## Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on April 11, 2025, the area sown under the summer crops is 66.97 lakh ha as compared to 57.49 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area of 31.50 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 27.55 lakh ha (increase of 3.95 lakh ha).
2. Rabi harvesting Status: As  on  11.04.2025,  74.82% of Rabi sown area has been harvested all over  India.  Approximately  97.00%  area  of  Pulses  mainly  in  Lathyrus  (99%),  Kulthi  (98%), Urdbean  (95%),  Moongbean  (95%);  80.56%  area  of  Shri  Anna  &  Coarse  Cereals  mainly  in Jowar (96.55%); 92.22 % area of Oilseeds majorly in Rapeseed & Mustard (94.71%); 51.04% of Wheat and 45.46 % area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25.
3. Rabi Season Area Coverage : For Rabi horticulture crops ,  major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion - 12.57 lakh ha (9.76 lakh ha last year), Potato - 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato - 3.20 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year).

## 4. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Gradual Rise in maximum temperatures by 2-4°C likely over Northwest India during next 4 days till 18th April and gradual fall by 2-4°C during subsequent 3 days. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over Central India during next 2 days and gradual rise by 2-4°C during subsequent 5 days. Gradual Rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over interior Maharashtra during next 5 days and no significant change thereafter during subsequent 2 days. Gradual Rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over Gujarat State during next 2-3 days till 17th April and gradual fall by 2-3°C during subsequent 4 days. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 14 April, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 24% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -42%; (ii) Northwest India: -43%; (iii) Central India: -1%; and South Peninsula: +85%. An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over West Rajasthan, 2nd over central part of south Madhya  Pradesh,  3rd  over  Gulf  of  Mannar  and  4th  over  southwest  Bay  of  Bengal  & adjoining Tamil Nadu and 5th over west Assam in lower tropospheric levels. A trough runs from cyclonic circulation over central part of south Madhya Pradesh to south Gangetic  West  Bengal;  2nd  trough  from  cyclonic  circulation  over  central  part  of  south Madhya Pradesh to South Interior Karnataka in lower tropospheric levels.

## 5. Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 11 th  April 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 66.82 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 37% of total live storage capacity (182.37 BCM).  The current year's storage is nearly 111 percent of last year's storage and 111 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period.

The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

- b) Groundwater Levels : Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014-2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.
- c) Seeds  and  Fertilizers :  For  Rabi  2024-25,  certified  seed  availability  is  337.98  lakh  quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
6. Pests  &  Diseases: Intensity  of  pests  and  diseases,  at  some  fields,  has  been  reported  to  be above  Economic  Threshold  Level  for  Coconut  (Stem  bleeding,  Ganoderma  wilt,  Rugose spiraling  whitefly,  Leaf  blight)  in  Karnataka.  The  Advisory  has  been  issued  by  the  survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level.

Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on April 11, 2025, the area sown under the summer crops is 66.97 lakh ha as compared to 57.49 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area of 31.50 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 27.55 lakh ha (increase of 3.95 lakh ha).
2. Rabi harvesting Status: As  on  11.04.2025,  74.82% of Rabi sown area has been harvested all over  India.  Approximately  97.00%  area  of  Pulses  mainly  in  Lathyrus  (99%),  Kulthi  (98%), Urdbean  (95%),  Moongbean  (95%);  80.56%  area  of  Shri  Anna  &  Coarse  Cereals  mainly  in Jowar (96.55%); 92.22 % area of Oilseeds majorly in Rapeseed & Mustard (94.71%); 51.04% of Wheat and 45.46 % area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25.
3. Rabi Season Area Coverage : For Rabi horticulture crops ,  major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion - 12.57 lakh ha (9.76 lakh ha last year), Potato - 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato - 3.20 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year).

4. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Gradual Rise in maximum temperatures by 2-4°C likely over Northwest India during next 4 days till 18th April and gradual fall by 2-4°C during subsequent 3 days. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over Central India during next 2 days and gradual rise by 2-4°C during subsequent 5 days. Gradual Rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over interior Maharashtra during next 5 days and no significant change thereafter during subsequent 2 days. Gradual Rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over Gujarat State during next 2-3 days till 17th April and gradual fall by 2-3°C during subsequent 4 days. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 14 April, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 24% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -42%; (ii) Northwest India: -43%; (iii) Central India: -1%; and South Peninsula: +85%. An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over West Rajasthan, 2nd over central part of south Madhya  Pradesh,  3rd  over  Gulf  of  Mannar  and  4th  over  southwest  Bay  of  Bengal  & adjoining Tamil Nadu and 5th over west Assam in lower tropospheric levels. A trough runs from cyclonic circulation over central part of south Madhya Pradesh to south Gangetic  West  Bengal;  2nd  trough  from  cyclonic  circulation  over  central  part  of  south Madhya Pradesh to South Interior Karnataka in lower tropospheric levels.

5. Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As on 11 th  April 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 66.82 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 37% of total live storage capacity (182.37 BCM).  The current year's storage is nearly 111 percent of last year's storage and 111 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period.

The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

- b) Groundwater Levels : Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014-2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.
- c) Seeds  and  Fertilizers :  For  Rabi  2024-25,  certified  seed  availability  is  337.98  lakh  quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
